record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Can one prove that there is no static spherically symmetric Einstein-Yang-Mills solution with non-zero electric field?

evidence.quote: (ii) show there is no static spherical solution with non-zero electric field;

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein–Yang–Mills system on a four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold with gauge group SU(2): the unknowns are a Lorentzian metric g and a connection (gauge potential) A on a principal SU(2)-bundle with curvature F, satisfying the coupled field equations
   Ric(g) − (1/2) R(g) g = 8π T(F),   d⋆F + [A,⋆F] = 0,
where T(F) is the Yang–Mills stress-energy tensor of F. A solution is called static if the metric admits a hypersurface-orthogonal timelike Killing vector field ξ and the gauge potential is invariant under the flow of ξ, and spherically symmetric if it is invariant under an isometric SO(3)-action whose orbits are spacelike 2-spheres, with the gauge action lifting to the bundle. In a standard gauge such a solution is described by a metric of the form
   −T(r)² dt² + R(r)² dr² + r² (dθ² + sin²θ dφ²)
together with electric and magnetic gauge potential functions; the "electric" components are those associated with the timelike Killing direction (the dt-part of A), and the solution is said to have non-zero electric field if these electric components give a non-trivial Yang–Mills electric field F(ξ, ·).

Prove that there exists no globally regular (or asymptotically flat) static, spherically symmetric solution of the SU(2) Einstein–Yang–Mills equations with non-zero electric field.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not turn up a definitive published proof that no static, spherically symmetric Einstein–Yang–Mills solution with non-zero electric field exists. Existing rigorous works (e.g., Smoller–Wasserman and follow-ups) restrict to the purely magnetic ansatz, while the vanishing of the electric component is typically imposed as a gauge/ansatz choice rather than derived as a theorem. The status of a fully general proof appears to remain unsettled.

status_evidence.title: Static spherically symmetric solutions of the Einstein-Yang-Mills equations
status_evidence.snippet: Static, spherically symmetric solutions analyzed under the purely magnetic ansatz (electric component set to zero).
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous existence results assume the electric component vanishes, suggesting the no-electric-field statement is treated as an ansatz rather than a proven theorem.

status_evidence.title: Classification of Static, Spherically Symmetric Solutions of the Einstein-Yang-Mills Theory with Positive Cosmological Constant
status_evidence.snippet: Classification carried out in the magnetic sector of static spherically symmetric EYM solutions.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent classification results also work within the purely magnetic ansatz, supporting that the general no-electric-field claim remains a stated open problem.
